prompt:
Estimate the crack-initiation life, in flights, of a lower wing skin detail.

**Stress history**
Each flight produces this sequence of turning points at the detail (ksi), ground to ground:

`-6, 14, 8, 19, 11, 24, 9, 21, 13, 17, 7, 16, -6`

Flights follow one another with the identical sequence.

**Data and practice**
- Cycle counting: rainflow (ASTM E1049), applied to the history as it repeats flight after flight, so that every counted cycle is closed.
- Mean-stress correction: Goodman with Ftu = 78 ksi, Sa,eq = Sa / (1 − Sm/Ftu) for Sm > 0; Sa,eq = Sa for Sm ≤ 0.
- Fully reversed S-N curve: Sa,eq = 95 · N^(−0.15) (ksi; N = cycles to failure). Cycles with Sa,eq below 6.0 ksi do no damage.
- Palmgren–Miner linear damage; failure at a damage sum of 1.0; no scatter factor.

**Report**
1. Rainflow cycles per flight
2. Maximum and minimum stress of the largest-range cycle
3. Damage per flight
4. Life in flights

Show your working. End with a single JSON object in a ```json code block, with exactly these keys and plain numbers:

```json
{"cycles_per_flight": 0, "largest_cycle_max_ksi": 0, "largest_cycle_min_ksi": 0, "damage_per_flight": 0, "life_flights": 0}
```
response:
Using ASTM E1049 rainflow on the repeating flight history

\[
-6,\ 14,\ 8,\ 19,\ 11,\ 24,\ 9,\ 21,\ 13,\ 17,\ 7,\ 16,\ -6
\]

and letting flights repeat so all residue closes:

## 1) Rainflow cycles per flight

Applying the rainflow stack logic to one repeating block gives these closed cycles per flight:

1. \(14 \leftrightarrow 8\)
2. \(19 \leftrightarrow 11\)
3. \(17 \leftrightarrow 13\)
4. \(21 \leftrightarrow 9\)
5. \(16 \leftrightarrow 7\)
6. \(24 \leftrightarrow -6\)  (the outer cycle; in a single block this appears as two end half-cycles, which become one full cycle when flights repeat)

So the **total is 6 full rainflow cycles per flight**.

A compact closure trace is:

- at 19: closes \(14\!-\!8\)
- at 24: closes \(19\!-\!11\)
- at 7: closes \(17\!-\!13\), then \(21\!-\!9\)
- at \(-6\): closes \(16\!-\!7\)
- repeating block closes the outer \(24\!-\!(-6)\) cycle

---

## 2) Largest-range cycle

Largest range is the outer cycle:

- \(\sigma_{\max}=24\) ksi
- \(\sigma_{\min}=-6\) ksi

Range \(= 30\) ksi, amplitude \(S_a = 15\) ksi.

---

## 3) Damage per flight

For each cycle:

\[
S_a=\frac{\sigma_{\max}-\sigma_{\min}}{2},\qquad
S_m=\frac{\sigma_{\max}+\sigma_{\min}}{2}
\]

Goodman correction (\(F_{tu}=78\) ksi):

\[
S_{a,\text{eq}}=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{S_a}{1-S_m/78}, & S_m>0\\[4pt]
S_a, & S_m\le 0
\end{cases}
\]

S-N curve:

\[
S_{a,\text{eq}} = 95\,N^{-0.15}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
N=\left(\frac{95}{S_{a,\text{eq}}}\right)^{1/0.15}
\]

No damage if \(S_{a,\text{eq}}<6\) ksi.

### Cycle table

| Cycle | \(\sigma_{\min}\) | \(\sigma_{\max}\) | \(S_a\) | \(S_m\) | \(S_{a,\text{eq}}\) | Damage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8–14 | 8 | 14 | 3.0 | 11.0 | \(3/(1-11/78)=3.493\) | 0 |
| 11–19 | 11 | 19 | 4.0 | 15.0 | \(4/(1-15/78)=4.952\) | 0 |
| 13–17 | 13 | 17 | 2.0 | 15.0 | \(2/(1-15/78)=2.476\) | 0 |
| 9–21 | 9 | 21 | 6.0 | 15.0 | \(6/(1-15/78)=7.429\) | nonzero |
| 7–16 | 7 | 16 | 4.5 | 11.5 | \(4.5/(1-11.5/78)=5.278\) | 0 |
| -6–24 | -6 | 24 | 15.0 | 9.0 | \(15/(1-9/78)=16.957\) | nonzero |

### Nonzero-damage cycles

#### Cycle 9–21
\[
S_{a,\text{eq}}=7.4286\ \text{ksi}
\]
\[
N=\left(\frac{95}{7.4286}\right)^{6.6667}\approx 2.39\times 10^7
\]
\[
d=\frac{1}{N}\approx 4.18\times 10^{-8}
\]

#### Cycle -6–24
\[
S_{a,\text{eq}}=16.9565\ \text{ksi}
\]
\[
N=\left(\frac{95}{16.9565}\right)^{6.6667}\approx 9.76\times 10^4
\]
\[
d=\frac{1}{N}\approx 1.025\times 10^{-5}
\]

### Total damage per flight

\[
D_{\text{flight}} \approx 1.025\times10^{-5}+4.18\times10^{-8}
\]
\[
D_{\text{flight}} \approx 1.029\times 10^{-5}
\]

---

## 4) Life in flights

Using Palmgren–Miner:

\[
\text{Life}=\frac{1}{D_{\text{flight}}}
\]

\[
\text{Life} \approx \frac{1}{1.029\times10^{-5}}
\approx 9.72\times10^4\ \text{flights}
\]

So the estimated crack-initiation life is about **\(9.7\times10^4\) flights**.
